title: Digital modes, packet and APRS
blurb: What CW, PSK, packet, APRS, FT8 and DMR are, and how checksums and ARQ keep data correct.

T8D01.why: Packet radio, IEEE 802.11 Wi-Fi and FT8 all send data digitally, so **all of them** are digital modes.

T8D02.why: FT8 is a digital mode built to work at **low signal-to-noise**, so it gets through when voice can't.
T8D02.trap: It isn't voice, TV or a repeater feature.

T8D03.why: APRS carries **GPS position, text messages and weather data**.

T8D04.why: NTSC is the **analog fast-scan color TV** standard.

T8D05.why: APRS provides **real-time tactical digital communications with a map** of station locations.
T8D05.trap: Voice-over-internet linking is IRLP or EchoLink, not APRS.

T8D06.why: PSK is **Phase Shift Keying**: data is sent by shifting the carrier's phase.

T8D07.why: DMR **time-multiplexes two digital voice signals** on a single 12.5 kHz repeater channel.
T8D07.trap: Position tracking is APRS, not DMR.

T8D08.why: Packets include a **header with call signs, a checksum for error detection, and ARQ** for retransmission. All three.

T8D09.why: CW is **Morse code** sent by switching the carrier on and off.
T8D09.trap: It's not a 2 m FM digital mode and has nothing to do with propagation.

T8D10.why: WSJT-X supports **moonbounce (EME), meteor scatter and weak-signal beacons**. All three.

T8D11.why: ARQ means the **receiver detects an error and requests a retransmission** from the sender.
T8D11.trap: ARQ is not encryption or compression.

T8D12.why: A mesh network is a data network built from **commercial Wi-Fi equipment with modified firmware**.
T8D12.trap: It's not a DMR voice mode, satellite system or internet linking protocol.
